title: Napkin AI Pricing 2026: Free, Plus and Pro Plans
summary: Napkin AI's pricing structure emphasizes credit limits rather than tiered features, with plans ranging from free to $12 per month.
body_markdown:
## Where Activepieces Fits Around Napkin AI Work


Don't expect Activepieces to lower what Napkin AI charges you.


It's an automation tool that chains apps into flows, and its free plan ($0, 1,000 credits a month, up to 5 users) can take over the repetitive steps around your visuals so the work you do pay for goes faster.


If a visual is quick to make but slow to prepare for, that's the cost worth attacking before you pay for a bigger plan.


### The repeatable steps around the visuals


When a visual recurs, most of the time goes into gathering and cleaning the source text, not into the diagram.


An Activepieces flow can watch a document or a form submission, pull out the text, tidy it, and hand it to you in a ready state, and a run is 1 credit however many steps it has.


Once the visual is finished, a second flow can post the result to a team channel and log a row in a spreadsheet, so you keep a record of what was made and who asked for it.


Picture the arrangement below: a document and a form feed one flow, which delivers text to a person, and a second flow handles the posting and logging afterward.


Napkin AI sits outside both flows. The takeaway is that automation covers the edges of the job, and the middle stays with you.


For the bootstrap version, you need nothing more than a free automation plan and a shared spreadsheet. The paid route only makes sense if you run enough flows that the tool's own limits start to bite, and that's a separate decision from Napkin AI's plan.


### What Napkin AI still does by hand


The steps around the visual (reading the document, cleaning the text, posting the result, logging the row) all run in one Activepieces product, so when a row goes missing there is one set of audit logs to open rather than one per tool.


The same product holds the agents, the 750+ integrations under an MIT-licensed core, and the controls (custom RBAC, SSO, SCIM, environments, git sync) that govern all of it.


Integration those together from separate point tools and you carry several vendors, several bills and several places to prove what happened. **Generation, styling and export remain manual steps** .


That matters for how you judge the plan. Automation won't remove export time or the effort of choosing between visual options, so those costs stay with you.


If exports, watermarks or volume limits are what slow you down, the answer is still a Napkin AI plan decision, not a flow.


Activepieces earns its place only when the preparation and distribution around the visual are what eat your hours, and even then Plus, at $12 a month for 10,000 credits, is the step up only if the free allowance runs out.
